To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a novel model that can learn to follow instructions and answer questions about a scene in the same environment and transfer knowledge between the two tasks by using a dual attention module.

(1) the Dual-Attention unit can be used for grounding words to visual objects and transferring knowledge between different tasks, and (2) the model can be used for zero-shot transfer of learned knowledge to new words in instructions by using object detectors.

(1) we present a model for visual navigation that can be trained to follow navigational instruction and answer questions in a zero-shot setting and (2) we show that this model is modular and interpretable.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following: 1. Can we leverage the power of multitask learning and cross-task knowledge transfer to improve visual navigation agents?
two main aspects of embodied language understanding: (1) learning to transfer knowledge across tasks and (2) leveraging object detectors for learning grounded representations.

the problem of knowledge transfer in the domain of embodied question answering and visual navigation.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we propose a model that can learn to navigate in 3D environments using language as a guide, and can transfer the knowledge of words and visual objects across tasks and environments.
the proposed method outperforms the baseline models on both the tasks and also enables zero-shot transfer to novel words.
our model learns to disentangle representations and transfer knowledge between two tasks, and is modular, interpretable and allows for zero shot transfer to new instructions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are proposing a model that can learn two different tasks (following instructions, question answering) and transfer the learned knowledge across tasks.

we show that a single model can be trained to learn both tasks, with the added benefit of being able to transfer knowledge across them, making it a more robust and interpretable model for visually-grounded navigation.

our model learns to disentangle and align representations of words and their corresponding visual objects across two different tasks, thereby enabling knowledge transfer between tasks and allowing the agent to generalize to unseen words.
The main takeaway from our work is that
by learning a disentangled alignment of representations, we can learn a single model that is modular, interpretable and capable of zero-shot transfer.
a multitask model that learns to align task-invariant representations can facilitate knowledge transfer across tasks, and improve performance in both tasks.

a single model trained on both tasks can learn to transfer knowledge of words and objects across tasks and improve performance on each task, while also being able to transfer to new words in the instructions.
